significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) law that an aligned LLM's refusal probability is "better fit by log(N) than by linear-N or by no-N effect," together with a supporting form-(ii) mechanism in which a "log-compressed count component" causally limits refusal and linearizing it restores scale sensitivity. This establishes both a consequential behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining expected refusal curves across unseen victim counts and explaining why large-scale harmful requests may not receive stronger refusals; HarmBench (Mazeika et al., 2024), StrongREJECT (Souly et al., 2024), and the refusal-direction work of Arditi et al. (2024) make benchmark coverage and causal refusal control concrete downstream decisions rather than merely topic-level importance. The branches are determinate and informative: linear or superlinear refusal would rule out scope-insensitive scaling, while an inert magnitude intervention would separately rule out the proposed numerical bottleneck even if the behavioral curve remained sublinear. In the topic-substitution self-check, replacing this count-dependent law with the generic goal of mechanistic LLM safety would not retain the score; the specific scaling relation, causal dissociation, and independently meaningful null branches put it well above the topic's default single-direction causal hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users two named handles: a benchmark "victim-count scaling axis" and the intervention "Magnitude-Linearizing Anchoring," with refusal-versus-log-count slope serving as a measurable diagnostic. Both can operate ex ante: evaluators can screen a model across harm scales before deployment, and the gated anchoring intervention can alter refusal generation before a dangerous answer is emitted, giving auditors and refusal-defense designers an action window. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—log-compressed severity and sublinear refusal across victim counts—rather than merely supplying a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction, although the asserted scope remains limited to aligned LLMs and count-expressible harmful requests. The topic-substitution check fails to preserve this reach: generic interpretability provides no such screen or defense, whereas this claim specifically tells safety-evaluation authors and deployment auditors what quantity to vary, measure, and gate.
